title: Smoked Salmon Benedict
subtitle: Poached eggs and hollandaise over smoked salmon and rye toast.
description: Poached eggs and smoked salmon with hollandaise on English muffins — lighter benedict for crews who want fish instead of Canadian bacon.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Smoked Salmon Benedict in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on. Use rye bread as listed — measure each before heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch Eggs. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Make dill hollandaise
steps.instruction: Blend yolks, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt 30 seconds. With blender running, slowly stream hot melted butter until thick. Stir in dill and hold warm in a thermos—not direct heat.

steps.title: Toast rye and prep salmon
steps.instruction: Toast rye slices until crisp at the edges. Arrange smoked salmon on a cold platter with capers and shaved red onion ready for fast assembly.

steps.title: Poach the eggs
steps.instruction: Simmer two wide pots of water with a splash of vinegar. Slide eggs in gently and poach 3–4 minutes until whites are set (165°F) and yolks remain runny. Drain on towels.

steps.title: Assemble the base
steps.instruction: Place toasted rye on warm plates. Layer salmon generously, scatter capers and a few onion slices over each portion. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 165°F at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Smoked Salmon Benedict onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Top and sauce
steps.instruction: Crown each with a poached egg, spoon dill hollandaise over the top, and finish with extra dill and lemon wedges. Serve within 2 minutes while yolks stay runny.

stationWorkflow: Keep salmon cold until assembly—warm plates only, not warm fish.
Poach eggs in two pots simultaneously to finish eight within the same window.
Hold hollandaise in a thermos at the line; never reheat over direct flame.
cleanupNotes: Rinse caper brine from prep surfaces promptly—it stains counters if left to dry.
Wash poaching pots with cold rinse first, then hot soapy water to lift egg whites.
leftovers: Smoked salmon benedict does not reheat well; cook to actual crew count.
Use leftover salmon and rye in a scrambled egg hash with capers and dill.
